item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $PQRS$. Sarika measures $\angle P = \angle Q = \angle R = \angle S = 90^\circ$.

Can she classify $PQRS$ as a rectangle without separately checking that opposite sides are equal?

options.A: Yes: a quadrilateral with all angles $90^\circ$ is a rectangle; opposite-side equalities then follow.
options.B: She should call the figure a right angle, not a rectangle.
options.C: Yes, even if $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ were only three rays and not a closed quadrilateral.
options.D: The same rule also classifies any open broken line of four right turns as a rectangle.
